instructions:
We're working on the code, located in ./src. Change the code so it does what the prompt asks, as the spec describes it.

The spec's Piton source is in ./spec. Don't change it, and don't read it to learn what the spec says: read the compiled reference instead, as above. If the prompt asks for something the spec doesn't describe, or describes differently, say so in your reply rather than working around it.

Before changing anything, write the constraints this task must meet to .suspense/history/1791092441-PromptHistoryNavigationAndEditing2.understanding.md, and keep it current as you read more of the spec. It is a Markdown list and nothing else: one line per constraint, at most twelve, each a single short, specific statement of what must be true, written as a link to the compiled reference file it comes from, such as `- [The chain tab has no bottom border in combined mode](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chain)`. Only list what the spec says; leave out anything you are deciding yourself. Replace a constraint when you learn it was wrong rather than adding another.

This prompt is the second step of a chain. Its first step changed the spec to meet it, and the spec has been built since. Now change the code so it does what the spec now says, without changing the spec. Follow the spec the prompt references, and the anchors the spec step names below. Where the spec and the prompt disagree, follow the spec, and say so in your reply.

The code is located in ./src.

The spec's source, which this step doesn't change, is in ./spec.

The prompt the chain was sent:

Up arrow in a prompt window should allow me to edit the last sent prompt.  If there's multiple in the queue, the queue list should auto expand.

What the spec step said it changed, its final output:

I've specced Up-arrow recall in the chat input, plus auto-expanding the queue list. `piton check` reports no problems, both files are formatted, and `piton build` succeeds. I confirmed both changes in the refreshed reference.

**How it works:**
- **When Up acts:** only when the chat input is empty, nothing is attached, no preview is showing and no menu is open. Otherwise Up moves the cursor as usual, and while the send menu is open Up still moves its highlight.
- **With prompts in the queue (Code, Chain, Spec and Freeform tabs):**
  - Up edits the **last queued prompt** through the existing edit flow, so Ctrl+Enter saves, Esc cancels, and the prompt is held while you edit it.
  - While you haven't changed the text, Up on the first line moves the edit to the queued prompt before it, and Down on the last line moves to the one after. Down past the last prompt cancels and leaves the input empty.
- **Queue list:** if the queue holds more than one prompt, editing via Up expands the list and keeps the prompt being edited in view as you move along. When the edit ends, the list collapses again, but only if Up was what expanded it.
- **With the queue empty, or on the Ask tab:** a prompt that has already run can't be edited, so Up brings back the last task sent, or the last question asked, as a **new prompt**. It comes with its attachments and its tab selected, and sending it runs it again. Up and Down step back and forward through the history until you change the text.

Two choices you may want to change:
- When nothing is queued, Up behaves like shell history and recalls past prompts. It could instead do nothing.
- Up only acts on an empty input, so it never interferes with moving the cursor through text you've typed.

## What changed in the spec, and the anchors the code should follow

- **`ChatInputShape.upArrow` (new):** handle Up and Down in the text input under the conditions above.
  - **Queue non-empty, on a task tab:** start the existing queued-prompt edit on the last prompt in the queue. Step along the queue with Up and Down while the edit is unchanged, cancelling the current edit first. Down past the end cancels the edit.
  - **Queue empty, or Ask tab:** load the latest task from the prompt history, or the latest question, as a fresh prompt with its text as typed, its attachments and its tab. Step through history while the text is unchanged.
- **`QueueListShape.placement`:** when an edit starts from Up and the queue holds more than one prompt, expand the list and scroll the edited row into view, following it as the edit moves. When the edit ends, collapse the list only if Up expanded it.
- **`ChatInputShape.editingQueued`** and **`QueueListShape.editing`:** unchanged. Reuse them for the edit itself.

56-<Up> in the text input, while it is empty, nothing is attached, no preview shows, and no menu is open to take it, goes back to the last prompt sent from the tab selected, as a shell goes back through its history. Anywhere else, as with text typed, <Up> moves the cursor as ever.
57-On the Code, Chain, Spec, and Freeform tabs, while the queue holds any prompt, it edits the last prompt in the queue, as editing it from the queue does, as Editing Queued says. While the edit is unchanged, <Up> with the cursor on the text's first line edits the prompt before it in the queue instead, and <Down> with the cursor on the last line the one after it, each cancelling the edit in progress first, as editing another queued prompt does; <Down> past the last prompt cancels the edit, leaving the input empty again. Neither goes past the first prompt. While the queue holds more than one prompt, editing from <Up> expands the queue's list, if it isn't already, scrolled to the prompt being edited, as the [QueueListScope](../queue-list/index.md#queue-list-scope) says.
58-While the queue is empty, and on the Ask tab, where nothing queues, <Up> instead puts the last prompt sent from that tab, the latest task in the prompt history, or the latest question asked, back in the input as a new prompt, as it was typed, with its attachments, and its mode's tab selected, with the cursor at the end of its text. It is not an edit of what was sent, which has run: sending it sends it again as a new prompt. While it is unchanged, <Up> on its first line goes back to the one sent before it, and <Down> on its last line forward to the one after, <Down> past the latest leaving the input empty. Once it is changed, <Up> and <Down> move the cursor as ever.

60-#### Preview
61-
62-Preview Compiled Prompt compiles the prompt as it would be sent from the selected tab, its hidden anchor, attachments, and mode's system prompt included, without sending it, saving it to the history, or building the spec first. In place of the text input, the chat input then shows what the harness would receive: the compiled prompt, as a sent task's compiled prompt is shown, beneath a row reading "Compiled prompt" with, at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to send · Esc to edit" (with ⌘ on macOS). While it compiles, the row shows a spinner and "Compiling…"; a prompt that fails to compile shows why, in the theme's error colour, in place of the compiled prompt. The preview grows with what it shows, up to 40% of the window's height, and scrolls beyond that. The tabs, attachments, and send button stay as they are.
63-The preview has keyboard focus. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS), or the send button, sends the prompt just as sending from the text input would, and the chat input goes back to an empty text input. <Escape> goes back to the text input with the prompt and attachments as they were, the cursor where it was. Switching tabs while previewing goes back to the text input too, since the prompt would compile differently.
64-
65-#### Tabs
66-
67-The tabs along the top of the chat input, one for each mode.
68-
69-##### Overview
70-
71-The input and buttons live inside the body of a tab bar, a flat strip 32 pixels tall on the ribbon's command area colour, #222222 in dark mode, with no line anywhere in it, whether beneath it, between its tabs, or around them. Each tab is only its label, in small text, with 8 pixels to each side of it and no border, and its label is always in its mode's colour at full strength, of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope), whether selected or not: Code red, Chain's icon purple, Spec blue, Ask green, and Freeform grey. The one exception is Chain selected, when Code and Spec take Chain's purple too, as the chain says. The selected tab is marked only by its background, the same surface as the body beneath it, so it reads as a tab joined to that body; unselected tabs have none, and show the strip, lightening a little on hover. There is a tab for each of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope), in their order: Code, Chain, Spec, Ask, and Freeform. Code, Spec, Ask, and Freeform are ordinary tabs. Chain is also a tab, just a small one, because it only shows an icon. All five sit flush against each other with no extra gaps, and no tab has more padding than a normal tab.
72-The chat input starts in the combined mode: Chain is selected, so Code and Spec are selected together, and a prompt sent before switching tabs changes the code and the spec together. Each open project keeps the tab it was left on, as the [OpenProjectsScope](../../open-projects/index.md#open-projects-scope) says, so a project starts on Chain the first time it is opened in a launch, and switching back to it selects the tab it was on.
73-Pressing <Ctrl+Tab> while in the chat input cycles from Code to Chain to Spec to Ask to Freeform and back to Code, <Ctrl+Shift+Tab> the other way, and focus remains in the chat input. It is <Ctrl> on macOS too, not <Cmd>.
74-<Tab> and <Shift+Tab> don't switch tabs, and don't indent the text either. They move keyboard focus out of the chat input to the next or previous control, as they do everywhere else. While the completion menu is open, <Tab> is still the menu's.
75-
76-##### Chain
77-
78-Chain is a tab with unusual behaviour. It shows an icon rather than a label, reading "Code and Spec" as its tooltip, and selecting it selects both Code and Spec. Its icon is drawn in Chain's colour, the purple of the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope), selected or not, as every tab's label is in its mode's colour. It never shows a focus outline, and its icon looks evenly spaced between Code and Spec whichever of the two is selected.
79-Unselected, it shows a broken chain dimmed to 50% opacity, and sits between Code and Spec like any other tab, overlapping neither of them.
80-Chain, like every tab, has no line along its bottom or sides, in combined mode or separate, since the tab bar draws no lines at all. Nothing draws a line beneath Chain and then hides it, since a hidden line can show again wherever rounding to the display's pixels uncovers it.
81-Selected, it shows a joined chain at full opacity. Selecting it animates as though it took a margin of -50% of its own width on both its left and right sides: Code and Spec slide together until they meet underneath it, so it ends up sitting on top of both. Deselecting it animates them apart again. While Chain is selected, Code and Spec both show as selected, one continuous background beneath the two of them and Chain, reading as a single unified tab. Chain itself has a transparent background, so the joined Code and Spec show through underneath it.
82-While Chain is selected, the Code and Spec labels are drawn in Chain's purple, the same colour as its icon, rather than red and blue, so the unified tab reads as one mode in one colour. Their colour follows the slide: as Code and Spec slide together, their labels shift from red and blue to purple, and as they slide apart they shift back, each reaching its own colour as the tabs settle.

27:#### Placement
28-
29-The queue sits along the bottom of the view, below the output and directly above the chat input, with a border along its top. It is not part of the header. A row saying how many prompts are queued, with a chevron, expands to list each queued prompt in order, a line or two of each, with a button to cancel it. Each prompt in the list is numbered, with its number, text, and cancel button vertically centred in its row, and the list scrolls once it gets tall, with a [ScrollbarScope](../../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope). Each time it is expanded, it opens scrolled to the bottom, on the prompts queued most recently, however it was scrolled when last closed. The same area holds the auto-send switch and the "Send next" button.
30-Editing a queued prompt from the chat input's <Up>, as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, expands the list while the queue holds more than one prompt, scrolled so the prompt being edited is in view, following it as <Up> and <Down> move the edit along the queue. Once the edit is saved or cancelled, a list it expanded collapses again; one already expanded stays as it was. The queue is shown only while it has anything in it.

32-#### Cancel
33-
34-A queued prompt that has not been sent yet can be cancelled, which removes it from the queue for good. A prompt already sent is no longer in the queue.

36-#### New Conversation
37-
38-Each queued prompt in the list has a small toggle switch, a slider, first of its controls, switched on while the prompt will start a new conversation rather than carry on the tasks', as its hidden anchor records, as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says. Clicking it switches between the two, saving the prompt again with the project. Its tooltip says which the prompt does, and that clicking does the other instead. The choice stays with the prompt wherever it is moved in the queue.
39-Prompts that will share a context are joined by a subtle connector line drawn between their switches: a vertical line 1 pixel wide in the theme's line colour, centred on the switches, running from the bottom of one prompt's switch to the top of the next one's, across the gap between their rows. A prompt that carries on is joined to the one above it; one that starts a new conversation is not, so each run of joined switches is one context. The first prompt in the queue is never joined to anything above it. Nothing else marks the grouping: there is no gutter, dot, or line at the row's left edge. The line follows the prompts as they are moved or switched, and is never under a switch, only between them. Each switch sits centred up and down in its row, however tall the row's text or attached images make it, and the line runs unbroken from one switch to the next across both rows' padding, with no gap where one row ends and the next begins.

The send button reads "Save", its tooltip saying it saves the queued prompt, and the send menu isn't offered.

Either way, the prompt that was set aside comes back just as it was. Saving an empty prompt isn't possible, just as sending one isn't. Editing another queued prompt meanwhile first cancels the edit in progress; so does switching projects.

Each prompt in the list is numbered, with its number, text, and cancel button vertically centred in its row, and the list scrolls once it gets tall, with a [ScrollbarScope](../../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope). Each time it is expanded, it opens scrolled to the bottom, on the prompts queued most recently, however it was scrolled when last closed. The same area holds the auto-send switch and the "Send next" button.
30-Editing a queued prompt from the chat input's <Up>, as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, expands the list while the queue holds more than one prompt, scrolled so the prompt being edited is in view, following it as <Up> and <Down> move the edit along the queue. Once the edit is saved or cancelled, a list it expanded collapses again; one already expanded stays as it was. The queue is shown only while it has anything in it.
31-
32-#### Cancel
33-
34-A queued prompt that has not been sent yet can be cancelled, which removes it from the queue for good. A prompt already sent is no longer in the queue.
35-
36-#### New Conversation
37-
38-Each queued prompt in the list has a small toggle switch, a slider, first of its controls, switched on while the prompt will start a new conversation rather than carry on the tasks', as its hidden anchor records, as the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says. Clicking it switches between the two, saving the prompt again with the project. Its tooltip says which the prompt does, and that clicking does the other instead. The choice stays with the prompt wherever it is moved in the queue.
39-Prompts that will share a context are joined by a subtle connector line drawn between their switches: a vertical line 1 pixel wide in the theme's line colour, centred on the switches, running from the bottom of one prompt's switch to the top of the next one's, across the gap between their rows. A prompt that carries on is joined to the one above it; one that starts a new conversation is not, so each run of joined switches is one context. The first prompt in the queue is never joined to anything above it. Nothing else marks the grouping: there is no gutter, dot, or line at the row's left edge. The line follows the prompts as they are moved or switched, and is never under a switch, only between them. Each switch sits centred up and down in its row, however tall the row's text or attached images make it, and the line runs unbroken from one switch to the next across both rows' padding, with no gap where one row ends and the next begins.
49:#### Editing Queued
50-
51-Editing a queued prompt, from the queue of the [PromptEditor](../index.md#prompt-editor), sets aside the prompt being written, its attachments, and the selected tab, and puts the queued prompt's text in the input, its attachments above it, and its mode's tab selected, with the cursor at the end of the text. Above the attachments, a row with a pencil icon reads "Editing queued prompt N", its place in the queue, and at its right, muted, "Ctrl+Enter to save · Esc to cancel" (with ⌘ on macOS). The send button reads "Save", its tooltip saying it saves the queued prompt, and the send menu isn't offered.
52-Everything in the input works as ever while editing, tabs included. <Ctrl+Enter> (<Cmd+Enter> on macOS), or Save, saves the edit, in the tab selected then, and <Escape>, when nothing else in the input takes it, cancels it. Either way, the prompt that was set aside comes back just as it was. Saving an empty prompt isn't possible, just as sending one isn't. Editing another queued prompt meanwhile first cancels the edit in progress; so does switching projects.
53-
54-#### Up Arrow
55-
56-<Up> in the text input, while it is empty, nothing is attached, no preview shows, and no menu is open to take it, goes back to the last prompt sent from the tab selected, as a shell goes back through its history. Anywhere else, as with text typed, <Up> moves the cursor as ever.
57-On the Code, Chain, Spec, and Freeform tabs, while the queue holds any prompt, it edits the last prompt in the queue, as editing it from the queue does, as Editing Queued says. While the edit is unchanged, <Up> with the cursor on the text's first line edits the prompt before it in the queue instead, and <Down> with the cursor on the last line the one after it, each cancelling the edit in progress first, as editing another queued prompt does; <Down> past the last prompt cancels the edit, leaving the input empty again. Neither goes past the first prompt. While the queue holds more than one prompt, editing from <Up> expands the queue's list, if it isn't already, scrolled to the prompt being edited, as the [QueueListScope](../queue-list/index.md#queue-list-scope) says.
58-While the queue is empty, and on the Ask tab, where nothing queues, <Up> instead puts the last prompt sent from that tab, the latest task in the prompt history, or the latest question asked, back in the input as a new prompt, as it was typed, with its attachments, and its mode's tab selected, with the cursor at the end of its text. It is not an edit of what was sent, which has run: sending it sends it again as a new prompt. While it is unchanged, <Up> on its first line goes back to the one sent before it, and <Down> on its last line forward to the one after, <Down> past the latest leaving the input empty. Once it is changed, <Up> and <Down> move the cursor as ever.

content.text:
Pressing Up in an empty prompt box now edits the last queued prompt, and the queue list opens by itself when it holds more than one. All 490 tests pass, including a new one that walks through the whole flow with real Up and Down key presses.

The spec says this applies to the last prompt in the queue. A prompt that has already run can't be edited, so with nothing queued Up brings an old prompt back as a new one instead.

**When Up does this:** only when the input is empty, nothing is attached, no preview is showing and no menu is open. Otherwise Up moves the cursor as usual, and open menus still use Up and Down to move their highlight.

**With prompts in the queue (Code, Chain, Spec and Freeform tabs):**
- Up opens the last queued prompt in the normal queued-prompt edit, so Ctrl+Enter saves and Esc cancels.
- While you haven't changed the text, Up on the first line moves to the prompt before it, and Down on the last line to the one after. Up stops at the first prompt; Down past the last cancels the edit and leaves the input empty.
- With more than one prompt queued, the list expands and scrolls to the prompt being edited. When the edit is saved or cancelled, it collapses again, but only if Up opened it.

**With the queue empty, or on the Ask tab:**
- Up brings back the last prompt sent from that tab (or the last question on Ask) as a new prompt. It comes with its attachments, its tab selected, and the cursor at the end.
- Up and Down step back and forward through older prompts while the text is unchanged. Down past the newest empties the input. Once you edit the text, the arrows move the cursor again.

**Two choices I made where the spec is open:**
- **What counts as "sent from that tab":** I only count prompts with that tab's mode that you typed and sent yourself. Steps the app sent on from another task are skipped: a chain's code step, a Send to Spec, a spec fix. Without this, a chain's code step (it has the same text as the chain) would come back on the Code tab.
- **Which edits can be stepped through:** Up and Down also step along the queue during an edit you started by clicking a queued prompt, not only one started with Up.

The chat input changes are in `src/chat_input.rs`, and the queue and history stepping is in `src/prompt_mode.rs`.
